name: Altek Electronics Inc (A Cyient DLM Company)
old_description: In addition to being the founder of Altek Company, a manufacturer of can testing equipment for the food and beverage industry under the name of Tech® Products, Steve is also the founder of Altek Electronics. Stephen graduated from UConn with a Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering, and earned a Master of Science degree in Electrical Engineering from Yale University. Earlier in his career, Mr. Altschuler was Vice President of Computer Dynamics (1963-72) and Manager of Quality Assurance for Adage Inc. (1959-63). He served on the Board of Trustees for the University of Connecticut from 1986-93 and is the former Director and Vice President of the Northwestern Connecticut Chamber of Commerce. In 1972 Steve established Altek, and for 50 years worked to create and maintain a business culture that emphasizes customer satisfaction. Stephen has worked successfully with his team to: create a loyal customer base; maintain a profitable business operation that pays its bills on time; and earn a solid reputation in the industry.
about:
Altek Electronics Inc., now operating as a Cyient DLM company, is headquartered in Torrington, Connecticut. The business was founded in 1972 by Stephen Altschuler, an electrical engineer with degrees from the University of Connecticut and Yale University. Altschuler previously held leadership roles at Computer Dynamics and Adage Inc. before establishing Altek to serve the electronics assembly market. The company remains under the leadership of the Altschuler family, with David Altschuler serving as chief executive officer.

The firm provides full-service electronics manufacturing, including surface-mount and through-hole PCB assembly, BGA placement, selective and wave soldering, wire and cable harness fabrication, conformal coating, and box-build system integration. Operations are supported by equipment such as the ERSA Versaflow 3/66 selective soldering system, a PVA6000 conformal coating machine with IR2000 curing oven, and automated component counting and barcode traceability systems. The facility employs more than 130 people and handles programs ranging from prototype runs to full-rate production.

Altek serves original equipment manufacturers in the medical, aerospace, defense, telecommunications, industrial/commercial, and transportation sectors. The company was an early adopter of AS9100, achieving “C” level certification and later upgrading to the “D” revision in April 2017. Its quality system is also certified to ISO 9001, ISO 13485 for medical devices, and IATF 16949 for automotive, and it maintains ITAR registration for defense-related work.

Altschuler’s founding philosophy centered on customer satisfaction, on-time bill payment, and a reputation for reliability. The company states it is dedicated to offering the highest quality electronics at the most competitive price without compromising its core beliefs, a principle that has guided its growth over five decades.
